rule: Friendly and calm, never pushy. No pressure or urgency language.
guideline: We talk like a friend who loves good food, not a salesperson. We never pressure people: no 'hurry', 'last chance', 'don't miss out', 'grab it NOW' or 'limited time only'. A simple call to action like 'shop now' or 'pick yours up' is fine.
bad: Grab yours NOW before it's gone!!

rule: At most one exclamation mark per post. Launch posts may use two.
guideline: Use at most one exclamation mark in a post. Launch posts may use two. Never use two in a row ('!!').

rule: No words in ALL CAPS, except approved acronyms and offer codes.
guideline: Don't write words in capital letters for emphasis. Allowed exceptions: MRP, T&C, FSSAI, and offer codes exactly as written in an approved offer (for example OATVIA20).

rule: No food guilt or body shaming.
guideline: Food is never 'good' or 'bad', and bodies are never a problem to fix. Never use 'guilt-free', 'cheat meal', 'junk food', 'sinful', 'skinny', 'burn it off' or similar.
good: A snack that fits your day.
bad: My guilt-free snack, no more cheat meals!

rule: Emoji limit: LinkedIn 1, Instagram 3.
guideline: Emojis are welcome but light: at most 1 on LinkedIn and at most 3 on Instagram.

rule: Product and brand names must be spelled exactly as approved.
guideline: Always write our names exactly like this: Oatvia, Oatvia ProBar, ProBar Choco Almond, ProBar Peanut Butter, Oatvia Oat Milk. Never OatVia, Oativa, Probar, Pro Bar or Oatmilk.

rule: Banned marketing words.
guideline: Never use these words, because they are misleading or not allowed for food: superfood, miracle, detox, cure, chemical-free, doctor recommended, doctor approved, clinically proven.
bad: A miracle superfood that detoxes your body.

rule: Use Indian/British English spelling.
guideline: We write in Indian English: flavour, colour, favourite, fibre, centre, litre (not flavor, color, favorite, fiber, center, liter).

rule: Prices use the ₹ symbol with no space: ₹99.
guideline: Write prices with the rupee symbol and no space: ₹99. Never 'Rs.', 'Rs', 'INR' or '₹ 99'.

rule: Units: number, space, short unit (20 g, 240 kcal, 120 mg, 100 ml).
guideline: Put a space between the number and the unit and use short units: 20 g, 240 kcal, 120 mg, 100 ml. Never 20g, 20gm, 20 gms or 100ml.

rule: Instagram posts must include #OatviaEveryday.
guideline: Every Instagram post includes our brand hashtag #OatviaEveryday.

rule: At most 5 hashtags per post.
guideline: Use at most 5 hashtags in a post.

rule: No rankings or superlatives without an approved fact.
guideline: Don't call us 'No. 1', '#1', 'the best', 'India's favourite', 'most loved' or 'healthiest' unless an approved fact with a source says so. Right now, no such fact exists.
good: A protein bar with 20 g of protein.

rule: Every number must match an approved fact exactly.
guideline: Every number we publish (protein, calories, nutrients, prices, discounts, number of stores or cities) must match the Fact Bank exactly. If a number isn't in the Fact Bank, don't use it.

rule: Environmental claims must match the approved fact exactly.
guideline: Following the CCPA greenwashing guidelines (2024), we only make environmental claims we can prove. The only approved one today: 'our outer box is made from recyclable paperboard'. The inner wrapper is not recyclable. Never say eco-friendly, green, sustainable packaging, plastic-free, 100% recyclable or carbon neutral.
good: Our outer box is made from recyclable paperboard.

rule: No health or medical claims.
guideline: Our products are food, not medicine. Never say they help with weight loss, boost immunity, prevent or cure any condition, are safe for diabetics, or are good for the heart.
good: 20 g of protein to go with your day.
bad: Helps you lose weight and boosts immunity.

rule: Diet and 'absolute' claims only where a fact supports them.
guideline: Words like 100% natural, vegan, gluten-free, sugar-free and no preservatives may only be used for a product when the Fact Bank says so for that exact product. ProBar Choco Almond is vegan; ProBar Peanut Butter is not. No product is gluten-free.
bad: ProBar Peanut Butter is vegan and gluten-free.

rule: Offers must match an active approved offer and say 'T&C apply'.
guideline: An offer post must use the code, discount and dates of a current approved offer exactly, and include 'T&C apply'. Never promote an offer after its end date.
good: 20% off with code OATVIA20 until 30 Nov. T&C apply.

rule: No comparisons with competitors or other foods.
guideline: Talk about what we are, not what others aren't. Don't compare us with competitors or with other foods (for example 'better than dairy milk' or 'unlike other bars').
good: Creamy oat milk for your chai.
bad: Creamier and better than dairy milk.

rule: Paid or partner posts must start with #ad or 'Paid partnership'.
guideline: Following ASCI's influencer guidelines, every post by a paid partner or influencer must start with '#ad' or 'Paid partnership' so people know it's an ad.
bad: My afternoon snack: Oatvia ProBar (no disclosure)

rule: Posts about ProBar Peanut Butter must say 'Contains peanuts'.
guideline: Any post about ProBar Peanut Butter must include the words 'Contains peanuts'.

rule: Main image colours must come from the brand palette.
guideline: The main colours of every image must come from our palette: Oat Cream #F5EBDD, Forest Green #2F5D3A, Deep Navy #1F2A44, Honey #E8A33D and White #FFFFFF. No neon or off-palette backgrounds.
good: Navy text on an Oat Cream background
bad: Yellow text on a neon pink background

rule: Text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).
guideline: Text on images must be easy to read: a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (at least 24 px bold or 32 px regular). Honey text on Oat Cream is not allowed.

rule: Every image needs alt text.
guideline: Every image needs a short description (alt text) for people using screen readers.
good: Alt text: 'A ProBar Choco Almond bar on a cream background.'

rule: Multi-word hashtags use CamelCase.
guideline: Write multi-word hashtags with a capital letter for each word (#OatviaEveryday, not #oatviaeveryday) so screen readers can read them.
